Its Li:anion ratio should keep it close to the sulfide, and B3+ is hard to reduce. proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (well above 2 eV) Li-ion insulator that is chemically compatible with sulfide Li6PS5Cl and has a PO4 framework that resists oxidation near 4 V vs Li. It is a widely used cathode/sulfide interface coating, so it is a strong first test of the penalty landscape.

Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap Li-ion insulator built from Zr4+, which is hard to reduce, so it should resist reduction by Li6PS5Cl. Its Li-rich oxide framework is also expected to be more compatible with the sulfide than the phosphate tested earlier, which gave P2O5/SCl4 products. It is a different family from the phosphate, so it is an exploratory test.
